Saying hello and goodbye

Four words are enough to greet anyone.

Ciao!Hi! And bye! With friends and family, when you arrive and when you leave.
Buongiorno!Hello, good morning! From morning until late afternoon.
Buonasera!Good evening! When you arrive, in the evening.
Arrivederci!Goodbye! The polite way, when you leave.

The trap: buonanotte (good night) is only said at bedtime. In the evening, when you walk in somewhere, say buonasera, just as in English you say \"good evening\" and not \"good night\".

", "

Thank you, please, sorry

Polite words come in pairs, like \"thank you\" and \"you're welcome\".

— Grazie! — Prego!— Thank you! — You're welcome!

Grazie mille means \"thank you very much\" (literally \"a thousand thanks\"). Per favore is \"please\": it never changes.

English has one \"you\"; Italian has a friendly one and a polite one. So to say sorry or get someone's attention: scusa to a friend, scusi to a stranger. And to answer: sì (yes), no (no).

By ear: ciao sounds like \"chow\", and in grazie you pronounce the final e: \"GRAH-tsyeh\".
